Would this work?

Mr. Fixer has out Driving Mantis, Jack-Handle, and Dynamic Siphon, and the Environment has Supercooled Trisolvent Vat.

1) Mr. Fixer plays Dual Crowbars

2) Supercooled Trisolvent Vat deals 1 cold damage to Mr. Fixer

3) Mr. Fixer redirects the damage to Dynamic Siphon

4) Mr. Fixer uses Strike with both Jack-Handle and Dual Crowbars

5) Dual Crowbars returns Jack-Handle to owner's hand

Repeat on next turn.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
I would guess with the new ruling on Crowbar that you would do a Jackhandle attack and each instance would use Crowbar to hit a second target based on the damage that just occured.

We already know that Jackhandle and Dual Crowbars do not trigger on the extra damage they create, or on friendly fire.  (Infinite loop no)

We know Jackhandle overwrites the original attack to hit all non-hero targets.

We know that Crowbars responds to the initial damage by creating a new instance based on the damage just dealt.

I think it makes sense that Jackhandle not triggering on friendly fire would work similarly with the second part of crowbars, and that crowbars would respond to Jackhandle the same way it would any other all-target attack.

I think Crowbars can, but I know Jackhandle was ruled that it didn't, because it causes a loop of beating everything but Setback.

Basically Jackhandle takes the attack Mr. Fixer (or klepto-Guise) would make and changes the targetting to "all non-hero targets."  Friendly fire adds setback's damage onto that attack, it isn't a seperate attack.

This language is all informal and rulings can change, but that's what I remember.

Would this work?Mr. Fixer has out Driving Mantis, Jack-Handle, and Dynamic Siphon, and the Environment has Supercooled Trisolvent Vat.1) Mr. Fixer plays Dual Crowbars2) Supercooled Trisolvent Vat deals 1 cold damage to Mr. Fixer3) Mr. Fixer redirects the damage to Dynamic Siphon4) Mr. Fixer uses Strike with both Jack-Handle and Dual Crowbars5) Dual Crowbars returns Jack-Handle to owner's handRepeat on next turn.

No.

Mr Fixer is not the source of the damage, he is redirecting damage from the Environment.

EDIT: Whoops!

Still no. The effects of the Vat happen before the card text triggers, you wouldn't have the second tool in play before you take/redirect the damage so Strike wouldn't trigger both tools as one of them is still in the "being played" space. If all text on them was active then you would have to return one before you used your power, as the return triggers when it enters play.
